text:
Anya: heads up — reproducible flake in the judge adapter when we run parallel quantized-runner jobs. looks like priming state leaking between concurrent judge instances. logs attached.
Liam: seeing this locally too. probable global cache / adapter singleton being reused across threads :/
Samir: can you paste the failing log snippet? or a minimal repro command?
Anya: repro command below, hit this in CI ~30% of runs on the quantized branch
```
./run_eval --model redwood-v2-q4 --runner parallel --jobs 16 --seed 42 --batch-size 8
ERROR judge_adapter: priming mismatch for anchor_id=23: expected hash=0x7f3a, got=0x2b9d
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "runner.py", line 412, in process
    adapter.prime(prompt)
  File "adapters/priming.py", line 88, in prime
    self._cache.update(kv)
RuntimeError: cache mutated concurrently
```
Anya: full CI job: https://ci.internal/redwood/12452
eval-bot: Build #12452 — test_judge_adapter_parallel FAILED (flake) :rotating_light:
Olivia: likely the adapter holds ephemeral priming state in a module-level dict. we should either make adapter instances per-eval or add an asyncio lock per-anchor.
Zach: long-term: avoid shared mutables. short-term: CI workaround: run judge adapter tests in single-thread mode and make them deterministic.
Liam: single-thread makes CI slow. better: create per-request adapter instance and reuse only read-only compiled artifacts. minimal patch idea: move `self._cache = {}` into instance init instead of module scope.
Samir: fwiw, quantization seems to amplify flakiness — we measured flip-rate uptick when q4 kernels switch. numbers: baseline flip 0.8% -> q4 flip 2.3% on Rubric-A/B pairs.
Olivia: we need clearer metrics in the eval dashboard: per-rubric flip matrix, tie_entropy, anchor_stability over time, and a per-model quantization flip delta.
Zach: tie-breaker heuristics proposal:
  1) if consensus size >= 3, use majority.
  2) if tied, pick judge with highest calibrated_confidence (temp-calibrated via isotonic on validation set).
  3) if still tied or low confidence, use golden-anchor fallback (deterministic seed) or return "ask-for-human".
Anya: for CI gating, can we require kappa > 0.70 and flip_rate < 1% on anchor validation? add a regression test that runs N samples with anchored paraphrases.
Liam: agreed. also add a synthetic-anchor test that stresses concurrency — spin up K parallels and ensure no cross-anchor contamination.
Samir: suggestion: compute Cohen's kappa and bootstrap CI; if lower than threshold, fail early. also log per-rubric confusion matrix so we can detect bias shifts.
Olivia: yes — and add demographic-balanced synthetic anchors to surface latent bias. e.g., 10 anchors spanning different dialects and prompts.
Zach: on dashboard, add real-time alert when quantized flip delta > 1% over baseline for a tracked rubric set. also surface kernel variant and bitwidth in the chart so infra/ops can correlate.
Anya: I'll open a PR that moves cache to instance scope and adds a minimal concurrency test. PR in ~30m.
Liam: please also add a CI job that runs the judge adapter test with `--runner parallel --jobs 8` and a short seed matrix to catch order-dependent flakiness.
Samir: could we add a small harness that computes "flip_heatmap" across anchors x models and push as artifact to the job? would make triage faster.
Olivia: yep — artifact idea is good. attach as CSV + small png in the job and link it in the slack thread on failure.
Zach: don't forget to include model_metadata: {quant_bits, kernel_name, compile_flags} in the logs — we need that to debug q-induced flips.
Anya: ack. will include model_metadata and a one-off script to run the heatmap locally. ping me if you want to pair on the patch.
Liam: once PR is up I'll run it against the flaky job 20x to verify stability.
Samir: also propose adding a metric 'tie_entropy' = entropy over judge votes when normalized; threshold where human review is required.
Olivia: agreed. tie_entropy + calibrated_confidence should feed into the rollout gating for new judge models.
eval-bot: new PR opened: https://gh.redwood/repo/pull/982 — "isolate-judge-adapter-cache + concurrency tests" — CI run started.
Zach: nice. once CI passes, let's add dashboard tiles and an automated alert recipe.
Anya: thanks all. I'll follow up in PR thread with repro script and test results. :white_check_mark:
Liam: thx — will help with stress runs.
Samir: great. rough plan: (1) patch to isolate state, (2) add synthetic anchors + bootstrapped kappa test, (3) dashboard + alert for quant flips.
Olivia: I'll draft the dashboard mock and the alert playbook.
Zach: 👍
Anya: closing the loop here — will post back with results.
